overview: Kazakhstan is the largest landlocked country in the world, stretching across Central Asia. Its capital is Astana and its largest city is Almaty. Kazakhstan became independent from the Soviet Union in 1991. It is rich in oil, gas and minerals, and the Baikonur Cosmodrome, from which the first person was launched into space in 1961, is on its territory.

geography.text: Much of Kazakhstan is flat steppe: vast grassland and semi-desert. Mountains rise in the south-east, around Almaty, and the west borders the Caspian Sea. Lake Balkhash in the east is half fresh water and half salt water, and the Aral Sea, which Kazakhstan shares with Uzbekistan, has shrunk dramatically since the 1960s.
